tour.title: Genesis 6:1–4: Sons of God, Nephilim, and the Flood
tour.intro: This tour walks slowly through the passage itself, then lets several teachers address its strangest phrases without pretending the interpretation is simple. You’ll hear both a spiritual-beings reading and a human-community reading, while keeping sight of what the paragraph is doing in the larger story: showing creation’s disorder deepening before the flood.

steps.why: Begin with a close reading of the paragraph and its immediate context. The teacher lays out “three main views” of the sons of God—spiritual beings, human rulers, or the godly line—and then carefully notes that the Nephilim are “not the offspring” of the union according to this reading, but are described as “mighty men of old” and “men of renown.”

This clip shows how the wording echoes Genesis 3. The hosts connect “saw” and “took” with the earlier fall narrative and argue that Genesis 6 is an inverted fall story: “spiritual beings who see that women are good” take them, so the passage portrays the sons of Elohim negatively rather than treating the event as morally neutral.
steps.episodeTitle: God’s Spirit in the Flood Narrative

steps.why: Hear a contrasting interpretation rather than flattening the debate. This teacher rejects the angelic reading because Scripture does not elsewhere present angel-human intercourse as a possibility, and instead understands the sons of God and daughters of men as opposing human communities—“the true church and the false church”—with the 120 years interpreted as the countdown to the flood rather than a lifespan limit.
steps.episodeTitle: 40 Minutes In The Old Testament: Episode 11

steps.why: End with the passage’s narrative function. The hosts say the point is not to solve “what occurred” biologically, but to show that the command to be fruitful and multiply has been reversed: instead of spreading God’s image, the world is “spreading a broken image,” and “things are spiraling out of control” as the flood approaches.

tour.closing: As you listen, keep Genesis 6:1–4 in view as a deliberately compressed and difficult scene. The teachers disagree about who the sons of God are and what the 120 years means, but they converge on the passage’s movement: human life is multiplying, power and desire are being grasped without restraint, and the good order of creation is being twisted toward judgment.

caveats: Clips on ad-inserted hosts (Megaphone: ask-nt-wright, spoken-gospel) can land up to ~2 minutes off against today’s stream. This is a known corpus-wide drift, not a bug in this tour.
A tour is model output over machine transcripts. The "why" text should report what a transcript says; it is not a claim that the speaker is right.

The player streams each episode straight from its publisher. A few hosts (Substack’s CDN, for one) refuse hotlinked requests and the step will say so and offer the URL instead — the clip boundaries are still good, the playback path is not.
